pending_selection.status: provisional - not confirmed, no implementation exists
pending_selection.hook_sentence_provisional: Lays out a book so no figure drifts away from the sentence that mentions it, and proves no other arrangement scores better under the rules you set.
pending_selection.summary: A standalone engine that decides all page breaks and float placements globally, minimising a stated editable cost (figure-to-mention distance, widows, orphans, page fill, spread balance), where shipping systems decide greedily page by page. The engine is the project; a book renderer and an interactive page grid with draggable, pinnable figures are its demos.
pending_selection.closest_prior_art: Mittelbach's two papers, both read directly on 2026-09-22 from open copies on latex-project.org. 'A general framework for globally optimized pagination' (Computational Intelligence 2019; DocEng 2016 best paper) is the global page breaker, and its base algorithm explicitly does NOT handle floats. 'Effective Float Strategies' (DocEng 2017) is the float half and the closer prior art: it already models call-out/float constraints, absolute versus preference rules, and the O(n^c) candidate-placement blow-up. Neither has been released; the 2019 abstract states that no prototype ever became a publicly available system. Tying a figure to its mention is therefore not a new idea and must not be claimed as one. Also: Bruggemann-Klein/Klein/Wohlfeil; Plass 1981 for NP-hardness; lua-widow-control and fewerfloatpages for the local, shipping heuristics; npm paged-with-floats for the greedy browser implementation of CSS Page Floats.
blocking_before_implementation: Re-read IDEAS.md section 4 after the gap (sleep-on-it gate) and answer the Gate E question written there: is the first public implementation plus verification plus interaction enough? Discarding is an acceptable answer.
Search PyPI properly (only name probes were done) and GitHub code search beyond line-breaking results.
Read the DocEng 2017 float paper itself, not only its slides, plus Bruggemann-Klein et al.
Read what Patoline, SILE, Typst and Vivliostyle do at page-break time, from source or docs.
Chase the pagination literature cited by Mittelbach 2019: Ciancarini 2012, Piccoli 2012, Hassan & Hunter 2015, Hailpern 2014, Holkner 2006.
Write NOVELTY_REPORT.md; confidence capped at Medium, with the method credited to Mittelbach at the top of the README.
Fix the name, then write definition_of_done and the milestone ladder into this file.
pending_selection.proposed_milestone_1: Vertical slice: one real document, end to end - global page breaking with float placement under a crude cost model, rendered as a page-thumbnail grid beside the greedy baseline from the same engine, with exactness checked against exhaustive enumeration on small instances. Proposed only; not a commitment until the ladder is written.
pending_selection.gate_b_environment_check: Verified 2026-09-22: pip installs work (fontTools 4.65.0, pyphen); real fonts under /usr/share/fonts; Chromium and ffmpeg under /opt/pw-browsers for rendering and animation; no TeX installed, so the control is a greedy page breaker inside the same engine rather than a LaTeX comparison.
pending_selection.originality_note: Scored 3 of 5, lowered from 4 after reading the papers: both halves of the method are published. What is unbuilt is a public implementation, exactness verification against exhaustive enumeration, per-break explanations, and interactive re-pagination under pinning. Whether that clears Gate E is the question the next run must answer first, and returning the candidate to the pool is an acceptable answer.
pending_selection.searches_closed_2026_09_22: npm, crates.io and CTAN registry sweeps; direct reading of Mittelbach 2019 and the DocEng 2017 float slides; prototype release status (no evidence of release; LaTeX project effort since 2020 has gone to tagged PDF and accessibility).
